findings.evidence: "Say it," he said. "You didn't see anyone."
findings.diagnosis: The repeated imperative plus the hand 'the size of the pane' reads as a man intimidating a witness — coercion, not desperation — weighting him toward villain. The exact ambiguity-tip the contract warns against.

findings.evidence: "Say it," he said. "You didn't see anyone." ... "There's a toilet round the back," she said.
findings.diagnosis: The man coerces immediately before she offers shelter, so her not-pressing reads partly as fear-compliance to him rather than a self-originated tangled choice.
